title: The go-live checklist
why: One page says what must work before companies sign up and pay, and what is still to do.
before: Signed in at the main site (operations.mghaiapps.com/login) with the platform owner's Master Admin account.

steps.do: Left menu → "Platform setup" (or Owner home → "Platform setup").
steps.expect: Heading "Platform setup", "… of 13 ready", and the Go-live checklist: cloud mode, e-mail, test e-mail, account & password sender, Razorpay keys, LIVE keys, your prices, GST decided, storage allowance, trial storage and logins, nightly job, Super Admin on its own address, self sign-up.

steps.do: Each line not yet done.
steps.expect: Says exactly where to fix it, with "Open →".

steps.do: Sign in as a company's own Master Admin and type /platform-setup.
steps.expect: "Only the platform owner (Super Admin), on the main site, can open Platform setup." — and it is not in their menu.

title: Platform e-mail — general sender and a separate account & password sender
why: The owner (22 Oct): e-mails sent automatically from our own address, with password e-mails from a different one.
before: Your mail provider's details (Microsoft 365: smtp.office365.com, port 587, mailbox address and password; the account address set up as a mailbox or as a "send as" alias).

steps.do: Platform setup → "Platform e-mail": Mail server, Port; 1 · General e-mails: Sender name, From address, Mailbox login, Mailbox password; 2 · Account & password e-mails: the same → "Save platform e-mail".
steps.expect: "Platform e-mail saved. Now send a test e-mail from each sender."

steps.do: "Send a test e-mail" — General sender, to your own address.
steps.expect: "Sent" (or "Failed" with the reason in plain words). The e-mail arrives FROM the general address.

steps.do: "Send a test e-mail" — Account & password sender.
steps.expect: Arrives FROM the account address.

steps.do: Sign up a test company (ONB-004).
steps.expect: The sign-up code and welcome come from the ACCOUNT address; later trial / storage notices from the GENERAL address.

steps.do: Inside a company with no e-mail of its own, send something (e.g. a quotation e-mail).
steps.expect: It arrives as "<Company> (via <your sender name>)"; pressing Reply writes to the company's own e-mail.

steps.do: A wrong password → test again.
steps.expect: "The mail server refused the mailbox login or password…" — in plain words, with the detail after it.

steps.do: Open "Recent e-mails from the main site".
steps.expect: Who, subject, Sent / Not sent with the reason. No sign-up code, password or reset link is ever shown or kept.

title: Payment keys check (Razorpay)
why: Before any company pays, the keys must be proven to work — without moving money.
before: Razorpay TEST keys from the Razorpay Dashboard → Account & Settings → API Keys.

steps.do: Super Admin → Advanced settings → Billing: paste Key ID and Key Secret → save.
steps.expect: Saved.

steps.do: Platform setup → "Check payment keys".
steps.expect: "Razorpay accepted the keys — TEST keys: no real money moves." The checklist line turns green.

steps.do: Change one character of the secret, check again.
steps.expect: "Razorpay refused the keys (wrong Key ID or Key Secret)."

steps.do: With TEST keys, buy a plan as a test company (ONB-047) using Razorpay's test card.
steps.expect: The plan activates; no real money moves.

steps.do: When ready: replace with LIVE keys (rzp_live_…), check again.
steps.expect: "… LIVE keys: real payments." The "LIVE keys" line turns green.

title: Super Admin on its own address, with its own sign-in
why: The owner (22 Oct): "Super admin shall have complete different login" — companies never reach the platform-owner screens, and the owner signs in somewhere else.
before: Signed in at the main site as the platform owner. Access to cPanel.

steps.do: Platform setup → "Super Admin address" → type admin.operations.mghaiapps.com → "Save address".
steps.expect: "Super Admin address saved. Next: create it in your hosting, then open it and lock Super Admin there." Three numbered steps appear.

steps.do: Still on the main address, look at "Lock Super Admin to this address".
steps.expect: Greyed out, with "Available when this page is opened at https://admin.operations.mghaiapps.com — so you never lock yourself out of an address that does not work yet."

steps.do: "Create it in cPanel for me" (or cPanel → Domains → create it with the same folder as the main site). Wait for the certificate.
steps.expect: https://admin.operations.mghaiapps.com/login opens the sign-in page.

steps.do: At the new address, before signing in, open /connect or /start.
steps.expect: Sent to the sign-in page — nothing public is served there.

steps.do: At the new address sign in with a company account or a member of staff.
steps.expect: "This address is only for the platform owner (Super Admin). Company users sign in at https://operations.mghaiapps.com/login."

steps.do: At the new address sign in as the platform owner.
steps.expect: You land on Owner home.

steps.do: Platform setup → "Lock Super Admin to this address".
steps.expect: "Locked. Super Admin now opens only at https://admin.operations.mghaiapps.com." The panel shows "Locked".

steps.do: In the OTHER browser tab (main address, still signed in) open /platform-setup or /companies.
steps.expect: Sent on to the same screen at https://admin.operations.mghaiapps.com (where you sign in separately). The menu shows "Super Admin ↗" instead of Owner home / Platform setup.

steps.do: Emergency: cPanel → File Manager → in exaact_data create an empty file "superadmin-unlock"; open /platform-setup on the main address.
steps.expect: It opens on the main address again; the Super Admin page warns that the emergency unlock is on. Delete the file → locked again.

steps.do: Try to create a company called "Admin" (or with the workspace name "admin").
steps.expect: Its workspace gets another name (admin-2), or "That workspace key is already taken — pick another."

ref: lib/superadmin.php superadmin_address_gate; lib/platform_mail.php; views/ops/platform_setup.php; index.php login

title: Your prices and GST — nothing built in, suggestions shown
why: The owner (22 Oct): "research this number and let me know or keep it open to configure in admin panel, don't hardcode it".
before: Signed in as the platform owner. No prices saved yet.

steps.do: Owner home → "Pricing" (opens Plans, pricing & usage).
steps.expect: Every price box is empty ("not set"). Under each: "Suggested: …" and the reason (evidence or judgement). A banner: "… numbers still to decide".

steps.do: As a company on its free trial, open Subscription.
steps.expect: "Plans are not on sale yet — prices are still being set." Nothing can be bought at an invented price.

steps.do: Back on Pricing: "Fill in the suggested values".
steps.expect: "… boxes filled — check them, then press Save". Only empty boxes are filled, highlighted; nothing is saved yet.

steps.do: Leave the yearly boxes blank, Yearly discount 20 → "Save prices".
steps.expect: "Pricing saved." The "Yearly price charged" column shows ₹9,590 for a ₹999 module and ₹4,790 for a ₹499 login.

steps.do: Tick "Charge GST …" with only a GSTIN and rate → Save.
steps.expect: "To charge GST, fill in your legal name, your registered address, the SAC code first. Nothing was saved."

steps.do: Fill GSTIN, legal name, address, 18, 997331, "before GST" → Save & push to all workspaces.
steps.expect: Saved. Platform setup: "Your prices are set" and "GST decided" turn green.

steps.do: As a company with a GSTIN in another state, choose a plan → pay.
steps.expect: Before paying: Price, IGST 18%, Total to pay. With a GSTIN in your own state (or none): CGST 9% + SGST 9%.

steps.do: After paying (test keys): Subscription → Payment history → the invoice number.
steps.expect: A tax invoice EX/2026-27/0001: your GSTIN and the buyer's, place of supply, SAC 997331, taxable value, the tax, "Total paid", "Tax payable on reverse charge: No". "Print / save as PDF".

steps.do: Companies → 💾 Storage allowance and 🚀 Self sign-up.
steps.expect: The same "Suggested: … · why" under each box (10 GB, 2 GB per login, 50 GB pack at ₹399; 30 days, 10 logins, 2048 MB) and "Fill in the suggested values".

title: A customer wants its GSTIN on the bill
why: The owner (22 Oct): "Suppose if customer wants bill with his gst number then??"
before: GST switched on (PLT-005). A company on its trial or plan, signed in as its owner.

steps.do: Subscription → tick modules → open "Bill to".
steps.expect: "Registered business name", "GSTIN — to claim input tax credit", "State — taken from the GSTIN when given", "Billing address", "Save these to our company profile for next time" — filled in from the company profile.

steps.do: Type a GSTIN with one character wrong → pay.
steps.expect: "GSTIN: That GSTIN has a typing mistake (its last character does not match the rest) — please copy it again from the GST certificate. Nothing was charged." What you typed is still there.

steps.do: Type the correct GSTIN of another state (e.g. Maharashtra) → pay.
steps.expect: Before paying: "Invoice to <name> · GSTIN … · place of supply Maharashtra" and IGST 18%. Your company profile now holds that GSTIN, its state and PAN.

steps.do: Pay (test keys) → Payment history → the invoice number.
steps.expect: The tax invoice shows your GSTIN under "Bill to" and "Place of supply: Maharashtra (27)".

steps.do: As the platform owner: Owner home → "GST invoices".
steps.expect: This month's invoices with totals (taxable value, IGST, CGST + SGST) and "Download for the accountant (CSV)" — B2B for GSTIN buyers, B2C otherwise.

steps.do: A customer paid WITHOUT its GSTIN and now asks for it: GST invoices → "Correct" → enter the GSTIN and "Why is it being corrected?" → "Save the correction".
steps.expect: "Invoice … corrected. The customer sees the corrected invoice from their Payment history; include it as an amendment in your next GST return." The list shows "corrected"; the invoice shows "Revised" and the GSTIN; the amount is unchanged.

steps.do: Try saving the correction with no reason.
steps.expect: Refused — a reason is required and is kept with the invoice ("Earlier corrections").

steps.do: Pricing → GST → SAC code "99731" → Save.
steps.expect: "A SAC code is six digits beginning with 99 (for software services usually 997331) — "99731" cannot go on a tax invoice."

title: Where a newcomer can start — the three front doors
why: A newcomer is one of three people: a company that wants its own workspace, a professional who wants work, or a company/agency that wants people. Each has its own door.
before: Signed OUT. A private browser window.

steps.do: Open the site address (operations.mghaiapps.com).
steps.expect: You land on the marketplace front page (/connect) when the marketplace is on, otherwise on the sign-in page.

steps.do: On the marketplace front page, read the three cards.
steps.expect: "I need to hire" → "Create a company account →"; "I’m a professional" → "Create a professional profile →"; "I’m an agency" → "Create an agency account →". Below: "Sign in as a professional", "Sign in as a company or agency", and a section "Get your own operations workspace" → "Start your workspace →" (only while online registration is ON). "Staff sign-in" at the top.

steps.do: Open the sign-in page (/login).
steps.expect: Heading "Sign in to continue"; Username, Password, "Forgot password?", "Sign in →". Links: "Go to the marketplace →" and, while online registration is ON, "Start here →". The line under it says to ask your office administrator for an account — staff never sign themselves up.

steps.expect: Heading "Cloud workspaces". If cloud mode is not on yet: "Switch cloud mode on" with a "Base domain" box — set it first (e.g. operations.mghaiapps.com).

steps.do: Panel "Workspace requests" → press "Online registration: OFF — turn on".
steps.expect: Message "Online workspace registration is ON — companies can now apply at /get-started." The button now reads "Online registration: ON — turn off".

steps.do: Signed out, open /login.
steps.expect: The line "Run an inspection company and want your own workspace? Start here →" now shows.

steps.do: Turn it OFF again and open /get-started signed out.
steps.expect: "We set up workspaces personally… Online self-registration isn't open just yet." — no form. Turn it back ON for the next tests.

steps.do: Note: when SELF sign-up is on (ONB-006), /get-started forwards to /start instead — the company creates its own workspace without waiting.
steps.expect: Opening /get-started lands on "Start your free trial".

steps.do: Open /get-started (or "Start here →" on the sign-in page).
steps.expect: Heading "Run your inspection company on Inspection Ops", ribbon "◆ Free during launch". Fields: Company name, Your name, "Work e-mail — we'll send your workspace details here", "Phone — optional", "Preferred workspace name — optional, letters & numbers" (with the domain shown after it), "Anything we should know? — optional". Button "Request my workspace →".

steps.do: Company name "TB Test Inspections", Your name "Test Owner", Work e-mail (one you can read), Phone, Preferred workspace name "tbtest", note "Testing onboarding" → "Request my workspace →".
steps.expect: A ✅ and "Request received" with three numbered steps ("We review", "We create your workspace and e-mail you how to sign in", "You sign in"), and that you will hear at the e-mail you gave, usually within one working day.

steps.do: Check that e-mail inbox.
steps.expect: An e-mail "We have your request for a … workspace" arrives (fixed 22 Oct — it used to send nothing).

title: Applying with bad or repeated details

steps.do: Leave Company name empty → Request.
steps.expect: The browser asks for the company name (or "Please enter your company name.").

steps.do: Work e-mail "abc" → Request.
steps.expect: "Enter a valid work e-mail address."

steps.do: Preferred workspace name "TB Test!!" (symbols).
steps.expect: Refused by the box (letters, numbers and hyphens only) — or, if it gets through, the name is made from the company name instead.

steps.do: Submit a second request with the SAME e-mail as ONB-002.

steps.do: Company name of 300 characters; note of 5,000 characters.

steps.do: Send 6 requests within an hour from the same computer, each with a different e-mail.

steps.do: Leave the page open for a long time (or sign out in another tab), then press the button.

steps.do: Open /start (or "Start your free trial →" on the sign-in page, or "Start your free trial →" on the marketplace front page).

steps.expect: An e-mail "Your trial workspace <company> will be deleted on <date>" — nobody has signed in for 15 days; sign in to keep it, or choose a plan to keep it for good.
One more warning each time; Companies shows the count.

steps.do: Someone signs in on day 40.
steps.expect: The warnings start over from that day.

steps.do: Day 90 with nobody signing in.
steps.expect: The company and its data are deleted; the owner gets "Your trial workspace <company> has been deleted"; Companies lists it under deleted companies with the reason.

steps.do: A company that has EVER paid, unused for 120 days.
steps.expect: Never warned, never deleted — it is view-only once its plan ends.

steps.do: Super Admin unticks "Delete unused free trials automatically".
steps.expect: Nothing is deleted while it is off.

title: A customer installs EXAACT on their own server
why: The other way to buy: a licence for one company's own server.
before: A fresh self-hosted TEST install (never production).

steps.do: Open the new install.
steps.expect: "Software Licence Agreement": full name, designation, organisation, work e-mail, three ticks → "Accept and continue installation". Missing fields: "Please fill your name, designation and organisation."

steps.do: "Set up the system": "Start now — one click" (or "Connect MySQL instead" → Test & save).
steps.expect: The sign-in page.

steps.do: Sign in as admin with the installer password.
steps.expect: Forced password change, then "Welcome — let’s set up your system", then the setup cockpit (ONB-030).

steps.do: Admin → Licence → "Paste the licence key MGH sent you" → "Apply the key".
steps.expect: The modules in the key switch on; others show as not in your plan.

steps.do: Without a key, with enforcement on.
steps.expect: A 14-day trial; after it the system becomes read-only, never locked.
